claims.text: Significant SRO suppresses lattice thermal conductivity in concentrated RHEAs between approximately 300 K and 1000 K.
The proposed suppression of lattice thermal conductivity is caused by enhanced phonon scattering at diffuse antiphase boundaries.
Above approximately 1500 K, thermal entropy reduces the effective energy barrier associated with diffuse antiphase boundaries.
At high temperature, SRO may have a neutral or slightly enhancing effect on thermal transport relative to a random solid solution.
A fully random solid solution has a homogeneous elemental distribution, maximized chemical disorder, and no local chemical correlations.
The random-solid-solution state of the proposed RHEAs has high lattice distortion.
MoNbTaW can be equilibrated into an SRO-containing state at 800 K.
Annealing at 800 K can experimentally induce SRO without causing long-range ordering or phase separation.
Rapid quenching preserves the anneal-induced SRO state for subsequent room-temperature measurement.
Locally ordered chemical clusters form diffuse antiphase boundaries at their interfaces.
Phonons disrupt local chemical order when encountering diffuse antiphase boundaries, and the associated energy cost increases their scattering cross-section.
Increased phonon scattering at diffuse antiphase boundaries reduces phonon mean free path and thermal conductivity.
The thermal conductivity of an SRO sample will be lower than that of the same-composition random solid solution below approximately 1000 K.
Above approximately 1500 K, the thermal conductivity of the SRO sample will converge with or slightly exceed that of the random solid solution.
SRO hinders screw-dislocation motion in MoNbTaW.
The SRO-induced strengthening effect on screw dislocations in MoNbTaW diminishes with temperature and becomes negligible near 2000 K.
The cited dislocation evidence does not directly demonstrate phonon–diffuse-antiphase-boundary interactions in RHEAs.
W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf has an order-disorder transition temperature near its irradiation temperature.
Formation of distinct precipitates such as Laves phases introduces precipitate or grain-boundary scattering that can dominate diffuse-antiphase-boundary scattering.
SRO-induced changes in local stiffness and phonon group velocity may compete with SRO-induced phonon scattering.

contradictions.description: The conditions require the SRO state to remain maintained during measurement, while the boundary places the order-disorder transition within the measurement range and the high-temperature prediction invokes thermal disordering. Above that transition, the SRO and RSS samples may no longer retain distinct structural states.

The intervention relies on quenching to preserve SRO, but the proposed ex-situ measurement reheats the quenched samples to 1800 K. This can alter or erase the prepared SRO state unless in-situ structural verification is performed throughout the thermal-conductivity scan.
